title: C482/643/2012 of OM TRADERS THROUGH ITS PROPRIETOR Vs RAM KUMAR SHARMA

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Criminal Misc. Application No. 643 of 2012
Om Traders. ÖÖ.Applicant.
Versus
Ram Kumar Sharma. Ö......Ö. Respondent.
Present:
Mr. Pankaj Miglani, Advocate for the applicant.
Honíble Alok Singh, J (Oral).
1. Mr. Pankaj Kaushik, Advocate, has filed his Vakalatnama
on behalf of the respondent, however, none is present
today on behalf of the respondent.
2. I have heard Mr. Pankaj Miglani, Advocate for the
applicant and have carefully perused the record.
3. Perusal of the record reveals that learned Magistrate vide
order dated 28.03.2011 was pleased to summon the
respondent accused herein on the complaint filed by the
applicant under Section 138 of the Negotiable
Instruments Act, 1881. Perusal of the record further
reveals that petitioner did not take steps for issuance of
summons to the accused respondent, therefore, complaint
was dismissed for non prosecution vide order dated
12.09.2011.
4. Mr. Pankaj Miglani, learned counsel for the petitioner,
took me to paragraph 3 of the petition and submits that
petitioner met with an accident on 10.09.2011 and
suffered serious injuries due to which he was bed ridden
and could not take steps for issuance of summons to the
accused respondent.

2
5. Mr. Pankaj Miglani, further contends that steps shall be
taken by the petitioner within such time as fixed by this
Court.
6. Honíble Apex Court in the case of Mohd. Azeem Vs. A.
Venkatesh reported in 2002 (7) SCC 726 has held that
complainant should not be left remediless, as he could not
turn up on the date fixed by the trial court.
7. Considering the totality of facts and circumstances, I find
that absence of petitioner, on the date fixed and failure in
taking steps for issuance of summon seems to be
bonafide, therefore, petitioner should not be left
remediless. Consequently, this petition is allowed.
Impugned orders dated 19.05.2012 and 12.09.2011 passed
by Additional Sessions Judge, Haridwar and Judicial
Magistrate, Haridwar respectively are hereby set aside.
Complaint is restored to its original number. Petitioner
shall appear before the learned trial court on 10.06.2013
and shall take steps to serve respondent accused on or
before 14.06.2013 whereupon trial court shall issue
summons to the respondent and shall proceed with the
complaint in accordance with law.
 (Alok Singh, J.)
 21.05.2013
SKS
